sanskrit: etad ākhyāya kākutstho bhrātṛhyām amitaprabhaḥ lakṣmaṇaṃ punār evāha dharmayuktam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Having related all this, Kākutstha of immeasurable splendour then spoke again to Lakṣmaṇa among his brothers, these words rooted in righteousness.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭhaṃ vāmadevaṃ ca jābālim atha kaśyapam dvijāṃś ca sarvapravarān aśvamedhapuraskṛtān
english: "Vasiṣṭha and Vāmadeva, and Jābāli, and likewise Kaśyapa, and all the foremost of the twice-born who are to be honoured at the Aśvamedha—

sanskrit: etān sarvān samāhūya mantrayitvā ca lakṣmaṇa hayaṃ lakṣmaṇasaṃpannaḥ vimokṣyāmi samādhinā
english: having summoned all of them and taken counsel, O Lakṣmaṇa, I shall release the horse, auspiciously appointed, with full concentration of mind."

sanskrit: tad vākyaṃ rāghaveṇoktaṃ śrutvā tvaritavikramaḥ dvijān sarvān samāhūya darśayām āsa rāghavam
english: Hearing those words spoken by Rāghava, Lakṣmaṇa of swift valour summoned all the twice-born and presented them before Rāghava.

sanskrit: te dṛṣṭvā devasaṃkāśaṃ kṛtapādābhivandanam rāghavaṃ sudurādharṣam āśīrbhiḥ samapūjayan
english: Beholding Rāghava, who shone like a god and was utterly unapproachable, they who had reverenced his feet honoured him with blessings.

sanskrit: prāñjalis tu tato bhūtvā rāghavo dvijasāttamān uvāca dharmasaṃyuktam aśvamedhāśritaṃ vacaḥ
english: Then, with palms joined in reverence, Rāghava addressed those most excellent of twice-born with words pertaining to righteousness and bearing on the Aśvamedha.

sanskrit: sa teṣāṃ dvijamukhyānāṃ vākyam adbhutadarśanam aśvamedhāśritaṃ śrutvā bhṛśaṃ prīto 'bhavat tadā
english: Having heard the wondrous and illuminating counsel of those foremost twice-born regarding the Aśvamedha, he became greatly pleased.

sanskrit: vijñāya tu mataṃ teṣāṃ rāmo lakṣmaṇam abravīt preṣayasva mahābāho sugrīvāya mahātmane
english: Understanding their considered opinion, Rāma said to Lakṣmaṇa: "O mighty-armed one, dispatch a message to the great-souled Sugrīva:

sanskrit: śīghraṃ mahadbhir haribhir bahubhiś ca tadāśrayaiḥ sārdham āgaccha bhadraṃ te anubhoktuṃ makhottamam
english: "'Come swiftly with many great monkeys and their attendants, for your welfare, to partake in this most excellent sacrifice.'

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇaś ca rakṣobhiḥ kāmagair bahubhir vṛtaḥ aśvamedhaṃ mahābāhuḥ prāpnotu laghuvikramaḥ
english: "And let the mighty-armed Vibhīṣaṇa of swift valour, surrounded by many rākṣasas who move at will, come to attend the Aśvamedha."

sanskrit: rājānaś ca naravyāghra ye me priyacikīrṣavaḥ sānugāḥ kṣipram āyāntu yajñabhūmim anuttamām
english: "And the kings, O tiger among men, who desire to do what is dear to me—let them come promptly with their retinues to that unsurpassed sacrificial ground."

sanskrit: deśāntaragatā ye ca dvijā dharmaparāyaṇāḥ nimantrayasva tān sarvān aśvamedhāya lakṣmaṇa
english: "And those twice-born devoted to righteousness who have gone to other lands—invite all of them, O Lakṣmaṇa, to the Aśvamedha."

sanskrit: ṛṣayaś cā mahābāho āhūyantāṃ tapodhanāḥ deśāntaragatā ye ca sadārāś ca maharṣayaḥ
english: "And the sages, O mighty-armed one, the ascetics whose wealth is their austerity—those who have gone to other lands, and the great seers with their wives—let them be summoned."

sanskrit: yajñavāṭaś ca sumahān gomatyā naimiṣe vane ājñāpyatāṃ mahābāho tad dhi puṇyam anuttamam
english: "And a very great sacrificial enclosure on the Gomatī in the Naimiṣa forest—let it be ordered, O mighty-armed one; that place is sacred and unsurpassed."

sanskrit: śataṃ vāhasahasrāṇāṃ taṇḍulānāṃ vapuṣmatām ayutaṃ tilamudgasya prayātv agre mahābala
english: "A hundred thousand cart-loads of choice rice, and ten thousand loads of sesame and lentils—let these proceed in advance, O mighty one."

sanskrit: suvarṇakoṭyo bahulā hiraṇyasya śatottarāḥ agrato bharataḥ kṛtvā gacchatv agre mahāmatiḥ
english: "Many crores of gold coins and hundreds more of silver—let the great-minded Bharata go in front, placing all these before him."

sanskrit: antarāpaṇavīthyaś ca sarvāṃś ca naṭanartakān naigamān bālavṛddhāṃś ca dvijāṃś ca susamāhitān
english: "The rows of shops along the streets, all the actors and dancers, the townspeople, children and the elderly, and the twice-born who are well composed in mind—"

sanskrit: karmāntikāṃś ca kuśalāñ śilpinaś ca supaṇḍitān mātaraś caiva me sarvāḥ kumārāntaḥpurāṇi ca
english: "and the skilled artisans and craftsmen learned in their arts, and all my mothers, and the princes and the inner apartments—"

sanskrit: kāñcanīṃ mama patnīṃ ca dīkṣārhāṃ yajñakarmaṇi agrato bharataḥ kṛtvā gacchatv agre mahāmatiḥ
english: "and my golden wife, worthy of initiation into the sacrificial rite—let the great-minded Bharata go forth placing all of them before him."

sanskrit: tat sarvam akhilenāśu prasthāpya bharatāgrajaḥ hayaṃ lakṣmaṇasaṃpannaṃ kṛṣṇasāraṃ mumoca ha
english: Having promptly dispatched all of that in its entirety, the elder brother of Bharata released the auspicious dark-spotted horse.

sanskrit: ṛtvigbhir lakṣmaṇaṃ sārdham aśve ca viniyujya saḥ tato 'bhyagacchat kākutsthaḥ saha sainyena naimiṣam
english: Having appointed Lakṣmaṇa together with the officiating priests in charge of the horse, Kākutstha then set out with his army toward Naimiṣa.

sanskrit: yajñavāṭaṃ mahābāhur dṛṣṭvā paramam adbhutam praharṣam atulaṃ lebhe śrīmān iti ca so 'bravīt
english: Beholding the sacrificial enclosure, which was supremely wondrous, the mighty-armed and glorious king felt incomparable joy and exclaimed thus.

sanskrit: naimiṣe vasatas tasya sarva eva narādhipāḥ ājagmuḥ sarvarāṣṭrebhyas tān rāmaḥ pratyapūjayat
english: While he was residing at Naimiṣa, all the kings came from every kingdom, and Rāma duly honoured them in return.

sanskrit: upakāryān mahārhāṃś ca pārthivānāṃ mahātmanām sānugānāṃ naraśreṣṭho vyādideśa mahādyutiḥ
english: The foremost of men, blazing with great splendour, assigned suitable and richly appointed quarters to those great-souled kings together with their retinues.

sanskrit: annapānāni vastrāni sānugānāṃ mahātmanām bharataḥ saṃdadāv āśu śatrughnasahitas tadā
english: Food and drink and garments for those great-souled ones with their retinues—Bharata, together with Śatrughna, swiftly distributed these.

sanskrit: vānarāś ca mahātmānaḥ sugrīvasahitās tadā viprāṇāṃ praṇatāḥ sarve cakrire pariveṣaṇam
english: And the great-souled monkeys, together with Sugrīva, all bowing humbly to the brāhmaṇas, performed the service of distributing food.

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇaś ca rakṣobhiḥ sragvibhir bahubhir vṛtaḥ ṛṣīṇām ugratapasāṃ kiṃkaraḥ paryupasthitaḥ
english: And Vibhīṣaṇa, surrounded by many garlanded rākṣasas, placed himself as a servant in attendance upon the sages of fierce austerity.

sanskrit: evaṃ suvihito yajño hayamedho 'bhyavartata lakṣmaṇenābhiguptā ca hayacaryā pravartitā
english: Thus well arranged, the horse-sacrifice proceeded; and the course of the horse, guarded by Lakṣmaṇa, was set in motion.

sanskrit: nānyaḥ śabdo 'bhavat tatra hayamedhe mahātmanaḥ chandato dehi visrabdho yāvat tuṣyanti yācakāḥ tāvad vānararakṣobhir dattam evābhyadṛśyata
english: No other sound was to be heard at that horse-sacrifice of the great-souled king but "Give as you please, give freely"—and as far as the supplicants were satisfied, so far was the giving by monkeys and rākṣasas to be seen.

sanskrit: na kaś cin malinas tatra dīno vāpy atha vā kṛśaḥ tasmin yajñavare rājño hṛṣṭapuṣṭajanāvṛte
english: There was no one there who was impure, wretched, or emaciated at that best of sacrifices of the king, which was filled with joyful and well-nourished people.

sanskrit: ye ca tatra mahātmāno munayaś cirajīvinaḥ nāsmaraṃs tādṛśaṃ yajñaṃ dānaughasamalaṃkṛtam
english: And the great-souled sages of long life who were present there could not recall any such sacrifice, adorned with torrents of gifts.

sanskrit: rajatānāṃ suvarṇānāṃ ratnānām atha vāsasām aniśaṃ dīyamānānāṃ nāntaḥ samupadṛśyate
english: Of silver, gold, gems, and garments being given ceaselessly—no end of them was to be perceived.

sanskrit: na śakrasya na somasya yamasya varuṇasya vā īdṛśo dṛṣṭapūrvo na evam ūcus tapodhanāḥ
english: "Not of Śakra, nor of Soma, nor of Yama, nor of Varuṇa has such a sacrifice been seen before"—thus spoke the ascetics of great austerity.

sanskrit: sarvatra vānarās tasthuḥ sarvatraiva ca rākṣasāḥ vāso dhanāni kāmibhyaḥ pūrṇahastā dadur bhṛśam
english: Everywhere the monkeys stood, and everywhere the rākṣasas too, their hands filled, giving garments and riches abundantly to those who desired them.

sanskrit: īdṛśo rājasiṃhasya yajñaḥ sarvaguṇānvitaḥ saṃvatsaram atho sāgraṃ vartate na ca hīyate
english: Such was the sacrifice of that lion among kings, endowed with every virtue; it continued for a full year and more, and did not diminish.

sanskrit: vartamāne tathābhūte yajñe paramake 'dbhute saśiṣya ājagāmāśu vālmīkir munipuṃgavaḥ
english: While such a supremely wondrous sacrifice was in progress, the foremost of sages, Vālmīki, came swiftly with his disciples.

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvā divyasaṃkāśaṃ yajñam adbhutadarśanam ekānte ṛṣivāṭānāṃ cakāra uṭajāñ śubhān
english: Beholding the sacrifice that appeared divine and wonderful to behold, he had auspicious leaf-huts made in a secluded spot among the hermitages of the sages.

sanskrit: sa śiṣyāv abravīd dhṛṣṭo yuvāṃ gatvā samāhitau kṛtsnaṃ rāmāyaṇaṃ kāvyaṃ gāyatāṃ parayā mudā
english: Joyfully he spoke to his two disciples: "Go, the two of you, composed and attentive, and sing the complete Rāmāyaṇa poem with the greatest delight."

sanskrit: ṛṣivāṭeṣu puṇyeṣu brāhmaṇāvasatheṣu ca rathyāsu rājamārgeṣu pārthivānāṃ gṛheṣu ca
english: "In the sacred hermitages of the sages, in the dwelling-places of brāhmaṇas, in the lanes and royal roads, in the houses of kings—"

sanskrit: rāmasya bhavanadvāri yatra karma ca vartate ṛtvijām agrataś caiva tatra geyaṃ viśeṣataḥ
english: "at the gate of Rāma's palace, wherever the ritual acts are being performed, and especially before the officiating priests—there it should be sung in particular."

sanskrit: imāni ca phalāny atra svādūni vividhāni ca jātāni parvatāgreṣu āsvādyāsvādya gīyatām
english: "And these sweet and varied fruits that grow here on the mountaintops—eating and tasting them, you shall sing."

sanskrit: na yāsyathaḥ śramaṃ vatsau bhakṣayitvā phalāni vai mūlāni ca sumṛṣṭāni nagarāt parihāsyatha
english: "You shall not come to fatigue, my dear ones, having eaten the fruits and choice roots; you shall accept nothing from the city."

sanskrit: yadi śabdāpayed rāmaḥ śravaṇāya mahīpatiḥ ṛṣīṇām upaviṣṭānāṃ tato geyaṃ pravartatām
english: "If Rāma, the lord of the earth, should summon you to sing before him as the sages are seated, then let the singing begin."

sanskrit: divase viṃśatiḥ sargā geyā vai parayā mudā pramāṇair bahubhis tatra yathoddiṣṭaṃ mayā purā
english: "Twenty cantos are to be sung each day with the greatest joy, with the many metres there, as was taught by me previously."

sanskrit: lobhaś cāpi na kartavyaḥ svalpo 'pi dhanakāṅkṣayā kiṃ dhanenāśramasthānāṃ phalamūlopabhoginām
english: "And no greed whatsoever is to be entertained, not even a little, out of desire for wealth. What use is wealth to those who dwell in hermitages and subsist on fruits and roots?"

sanskrit: yadi pṛcchet sa kākutstho yuvāṃ kasyeti dārakau vālmīker atha śiṣyau hi brūtām evaṃ narādhipam
english: "If Kākutstha should ask you, 'Children, of whom are you?', say to the lord of men: 'We are disciples of Vālmīki.'"

sanskrit: imās tantrīḥ sumadhurāḥ sthānaṃ vā pūrvadarśitam mūrchayitvā sumadhuraṃ gāyetāṃ vigatajvarau
english: "Having attuned these strings to the sweetest pitch, or the mode shown before, sing with utmost sweetness, free from anxiety."

sanskrit: ādiprabhṛti geyaṃ syān na cāvajñāya pārthivam pitā hi sarvabhūtānāṃ rājā bhavati dharmataḥ
english: "The singing should proceed from the beginning, and without disrespecting the king; for the king is by right the father of all beings."

sanskrit: tad yuvāṃ hṛṣṭamanasau śvaḥ prabhāte samādhinā gāyetāṃ madhuraṃ geyaṃ tantrīlayasamanvitam
english: "Therefore, the two of you, with joyful hearts, sing tomorrow at dawn with full concentration the sweet song accompanied by the melody of the lute."

sanskrit: iti saṃdiśya bahuśo muniḥ prācetasas tadā vālmīkiḥ paramodāras tūṣṇīm āsīn mahāyaśāḥ
english: Having instructed them thus many times, the sage Prācetasa, Vālmīki of surpassing generosity and great renown, then fell silent.

sanskrit: tām adbhutāṃ tau hṛdaye kumārau niveśya vāṇīm ṛṣibhāṣitāṃ śubhām samutsukau tau sukham ūṣatur niśāṃ yathāśvinau bhārgavanītisaṃskṛtau
english: The two princes, having placed that wondrous and auspicious instruction of the sage within their hearts, passed the night happily and with eager anticipation, even as the two Aśvins refined by the teaching of Bhārgava.
